key_insight: Fluid‑centric PDE foundation models do not reliably generalize to extreme‑loading material dynamics dominated by shocks, interfaces, and fracture; systematic out‑of‑distribution benchmarking on two discontinuity regimes (PLI and FRAC) reveals where transfer succeeds and where adaptation is needed.
problem_solved: Addresses the uncertainty about whether PDE models pretrained on fluid benchmarks can be applied to highly non‑smooth, discontinuity‑dominated material dynamics under extreme loading, and provides a benchmark to quantify out‑of‑distribution transfer.
method: Take PDE foundation models pretrained on fluid‑centric datasets and evaluate their out‑of‑distribution performance on two material regimes: perturbed layered interfaces (PLI) and dynamic fracture/failure (FRAC).

Formulate a downstream prediction task focused on terminal (final) state / key outcome prediction for those regimes and measure model accuracy and failure modes under shocks, evolving interfaces, and fracture.
Analyze results to identify robustness gaps and guide targeted adaptation strategies (e.g., data augmentation, physics‑aware loss, or fine‑tuning on discontinuous phenomena).
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a clear benchmark and failure‑mode map for applying PDE foundation models outside fluid domains, informing safer deployment and focused domain‑adaptation strategies for material dynamics under extreme loading.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained PDE model → OOD evaluation → PLI and FRAC testbeds → terminal‑state metrics
Side‑by‑side visuals of PLI vs FRAC: snapshots showing shocks, interfaces, and fractures (heatmap/contour images)
Bar/box charts comparing model performance and error distributions across in‑domain (fluid) vs OOD (PLI, FRAC) cases highlighting failure modes
Icon set: shock wave, material interface, crack/fracture, and a transfer/adaptation gear to convey domain shift and remedies
paper_title: Out-of-distribution transfer of PDE foundation models to material dynamics under extreme loading
paper_authors: Mahindra Rautela, Alexander Most, Siddharth Mansingh, Aleksandra Pachalieva, Bradley Love
